clinician.trajectory_summary: A 46-year-old male presented with a 2-year history of progressive gait disorder, poor balance, and neurological signs including horizontal nystagmus, intention tremor, and ataxic gait. Routine labs and thyroid function were normal, but anti-thyroid antibodies were elevated. Brain MRI revealed bilateral cerebellar atrophy in the superior vermis. Paraneoplastic onconeural antibodies tested negative. Imaging via PET/CT revealed a hypermetabolic thyroid nodule. Biopsy classified the nodule as Bethesda category V, indicating suspected papillary thyroid carcinoma. The temporal relationship of neurological symptoms with cancer diagnosis supported a definite PNS diagnosis despite negative antibodies.
